decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The outside MRI covers the whole thigh mass. A central part is bright on the precontrast T1 sequence, which has no fat suppression. The supplied postcontrast T1 sequence uses fat suppression; fluid-sensitive images also show bright areas. The team is completing the local MRI record before tissue sampling.
decisionNodes.stem: Which additional MRI comparison should be obtained for {patientName}'s biopsy planning?

answerChoices.label: Axial T1 before and after contrast, both with fat suppression
answerChoices.rationale: A comparison with consistent sequence settings can distinguish intrinsic precontrast brightness from contrast-related change. The outside pair changes both contrast status and suppression, so brightness differences cannot simply be assigned to enhancement.

answerChoices.label: Axial and coronal T1 after contrast, both with fat suppression
answerChoices.rationale: Orthogonal anatomy is useful, but two postcontrast views do not supply a comparable precontrast baseline for the intrinsically bright area.

answerChoices.label: Axial T1 without fat suppression and fluid-sensitive images before contrast
answerChoices.rationale: These contribute tissue characterization but retain an unsuppressed T1 baseline. Different sequence weighting does not supply the comparable pre/postcontrast information needed for this targeting question.

decisionNodes.explanation: Signal differences must be interpreted against how the images were acquired. A bright native T1 region and a postcontrast image with a different suppression setting cannot simply be compared as if contrast were their only difference. Comparable before/after acquisitions can clarify enhancement for the later planning report.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial tissue-sampling plan should the sarcoma team select for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy of region A along path A
answerChoices.rationale: Obtains diagnostic cores from viable tissue while keeping the planned tract within the tumor-bearing compartment.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy of region B along path B
answerChoices.rationale: Selects the shorter route to the more intensely enhancing region but contaminates a separate muscle compartment.

answerChoices.label: Open incisional biopsy of region A along path A
answerChoices.rationale: Uses the better tract but escalates to an open procedure before a feasible initial core approach has been attempted.

answerChoices.label: Open incisional biopsy of region B along path B
answerChoices.rationale: Combines premature open sampling with the path that traverses a separate muscle compartment.

decisionNodes.explanation: Plan the biopsy with the team that would perform definitive surgery. Both offered targets are viable, so the most intense enhancement/shortest route is not sufficient: preserve the surgical approach and avoid traversing a separate compartment. A feasible image-guided core approach is preferred initially; open biopsy is a selected alternative rather than automatically wrong. Both method and tract are balanced across the offered plans.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The acquisition log records T1 and fluid-sensitive upper-arm series and no administered contrast. Several internal regions have similarly bright signal on the fluid-sensitive images.
decisionNodes.stem: Which acquisition should guide selection of {patientName}'s biopsy target?

answerChoices.label: MRI before and after contrast to map internal enhancement
answerChoices.rationale: Enhancement can help distinguish viable tissue for targeting when fluid-sensitive brightness does not establish which regions are solid.

answerChoices.label: Higher-resolution fluid-sensitive MRI to map internal signal
answerChoices.rationale: More spatial detail in the same fluid-sensitive appearance does not itself establish viability of similarly bright regions.

answerChoices.label: FDG PET/CT to map internal metabolic uptake
answerChoices.rationale: Metabolic targeting can be useful selectively, but is not the initial local MRI acquisition used here to distinguish internal viable tissue before planned biopsy.

decisionNodes.explanation: The administration log establishes that post-contrast data were not merely omitted from an export. When fluid-sensitive signal does not distinguish internal components, contrast-enhanced local MRI can help identify viable tissue for representative targeting. Increasing resolution of the same signal contrast or substituting a metabolic study answers a different planning question. No signal threshold or contrast dose is taught.

decisionNodes.stem: Which repeat neck-node sampling request should be made for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Peripheral tissue: cytology and thyroglobulin washout
answerChoices.rationale: The sampled fluid did not represent the suspicious tissue. Representative nodal cytology with selected thyroglobulin washout addresses the thyroid-metastasis question; use a nodal approach that avoids thyroid contamination.

answerChoices.label: Central cyst fluid: cytology and thyroglobulin washout
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating a relevant assay on the same nonrepresentative compartment can reproduce an uninterpretable result rather than resolve the tissue/morphology discordance.

answerChoices.label: Peripheral tissue: cytology and flow cytometry
answerChoices.rationale: This targets tissue, but flow cytometry addresses a different competing lymphoid process; it is not the preferred adjunct for this thyroid-cancer nodal question.

answerChoices.label: Central cyst fluid: cytology and flow cytometry
answerChoices.rationale: Both the sampled compartment and ancillary test leave the thyroid-related nodal concern inadequately assessed.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: {patientName} was born at 26 weeks and remains in an outside neonatal unit. Discharge is being planned with ongoing respiratory follow-up.
decisionNodes.stem: Which repair-timing plan is most appropriate for {patientName}'s current groin finding?

answerChoices.label: Plan repair after the neonatal hospitalization
answerChoices.rationale: For a currently reducible hernia in a very preterm infant with ongoing respiratory disease, a delayed planned repair with follow-up is reasonable. The timing balances respiratory risk against incarceration during the wait; it is not indefinite observation or a universal age rule.

answerChoices.label: Plan repair before neonatal discharge
answerChoices.rationale: Earlier repair limits the time exposed to incarceration risk, but carries respiratory tradeoffs in this infant. No current incarceration complication requires overriding the respiratory consideration in the offered comparison.

answerChoices.label: Use serial surveillance for spontaneous resolution
answerChoices.rationale: The current record repeatedly demonstrates a hernia, rather than documented resolution. Its reducibility supports a planned timing discussion, not a presumption that repair will become unnecessary. Reassessment remains part of the delayed surgical plan.

decisionNodes.explanation: For a currently reducible hernia in a very preterm infant with ongoing respiratory disease, a delayed planned repair with follow-up is reasonable. items.label: Groin course
items.value: Pediatric surgical examinations repeatedly show an inguinal bulge that reduces completely. There have been no painful irreducible episodes, vomiting or skin changes.

items.label: Respiratory and follow-up context
items.value: He still needs oxygen for bronchopulmonary dysplasia. His family can attend surgical follow-up and has been taught the warning signs requiring urgent reassessment.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The referring team asks about the repair sequence. She remains intubated on conventional ventilation; the chest radiograph still shows bowel in the left hemithorax.
decisionNodes.stem: Which repair-sequencing plan is best supported by {patientName}'s current outside ICU record?

answerChoices.label: Plan repair while continuing the present ICU support
answerChoices.rationale: Respiratory, perfusion and pressure trajectories support multidisciplinary repair assessment despite residual pulmonary hypertension and intubation.

answerChoices.label: Continue stabilization before reconsidering the repair
answerChoices.rationale: This fits ongoing instability, but intubation and residual sub-systemic pulmonary hypertension do not by themselves outweigh the current trajectory.

answerChoices.label: Assess ECMO escalation before planning the repair
answerChoices.rationale: ECMO assessment is relevant to instability despite maximal support, which this record does not show.

decisionNodes.explanation: Persistent hernia and intubation do not themselves determine timing. Interpret the whole trend: perfusion and oxygenation have been sustained and estimated pulmonary pressure is now below systemic. The current CAHS guideline supports considering repair after physiological readiness is sustained, with the neonatal, surgical and anesthesia teams confirming the plan. This is not automatic operative clearance or a guarantee of safety; renewed instability would change the sequence.
